body:
UI for Aman's projects must use volt-web, his shadcn-derived compact design system at /Volumes/D/www/projects/khanakia/volt/volt-web — not hand-rolled components.

What to take: src/components/ui/*.tsx (Base UI primitives + CVA variants), src/lib/utils.ts (cn), and the density tokens from src/styles.css. The tokens are the heart of it: --control-height 28px, --control-padding-x 10px, --control-font-size 12px, --row-padding-y 6px, --row-font-size 13px. Every control and row reads them, so changing one value rescales the whole UI in lockstep.

Taste it encodes: Polaris-grade density, flat black primary with no drop shadow and an active-press, outline buttons as a 1px frame, button sizes xs=24px for row actions and default=28px, destructive-outline for inline deletes.

What Aman called "one of the worst UX you ever build": hand-rolled primitives, lowercase text buttons stacked four-per-row, loose spacing, no icons, no overflow menus. The fix is two real buttons plus a DropdownMenu, coloured state pills, real Tabs/Table/Switch, and lucide icons.

Also: a UI bug can pass every unit test. The redesigned row put four things on one line and they overlapped at 420px; the tests assert content and callbacks, not geometry. Render the surface and look at it before calling it done.
